overview: Yidu Tech is a Hong Kong-listed, Beijing-headquartered medical big-data and AI company that has built YiduCore, a proprietary healthcare data and AI platform trained on nearly 9 billion authorized real-world medical records covering over 1.3 billion patient visits across more than 12,000 Chinese hospitals. The Group monetizes this data/AI infrastructure through three segments -- AI for Medical (hospital/regulator data platforms), AI for Life Sciences (CRO-like real-world evidence and clinical research services for pharma), and AI for Care (health-insurance/Hui Min Bao operation and chronic-disease management) -- and operates almost exclusively within mainland China's public and private healthcare ecosystem. The company reports in RMB with a 31 March fiscal year-end and achieved its first full-year net profit in FY2026 (ended 31 March 2026) after six years as a loss-making, cash-burning growth story.

business_model.summary: Yidu Tech sells data-intelligence platforms, AI-enabled software/solutions and services built on its YiduCore data/knowledge-graph/LLM stack to three customer groups: hospitals and health regulators (project- and subscription-like platform deployments), pharmaceutical/biotech/medtech companies (real-world evidence generation and CRO-style clinical research services), and health insurers/city governments (operating city-level 'Hui Min Bao' inclusive supplementary health insurance programs and digital therapeutics). Revenue is a mix of project-based system/platform delivery (AI for Medical), service/project fees tied to clinical study volume (AI for Life Sciences), and operating/service fees tied to insured population and transaction volume (AI for Care); management is explicitly trying to shift the mix toward reusable, disease-based platform/subscription revenue rather than one-off projects.

revenue_streams.name: AI for Medical (Big Data Platform and Solutions)
AI for Life Sciences (Life Sciences Solutions)
revenue_streams.trend: growing modestly, segment revenue dipped in H1 FY2026

revenue_streams.name: AI for Care (Health Management Platform and Solutions)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2G: top-tier hospitals (133 clients), health regulators/policymakers (54 clients), multinational and domestic pharma/biotech/medtech companies (98 life-science clients, 17 of top 20 MNC pharma), and municipal governments/insurers for Hui Min Bao programs (tens of millions of insured/active users)
business_model.geographic_mix: Almost entirely mainland China; company states intent to explore overseas/international replication of its disease-based and outcome-based platform model as a 'second growth curve,' but this is nascent and not yet a reported revenue line

main_competitors: Donghua Software/東華軟件 healthcare units
Global life-sciences data/CRO players (IQVIA, Medidata) in the life-sciences segment
Various regional/public hospital information system vendors
competitive_position.market_position: Per Frost & Sullivan data cited in earlier filings, Yidu ranked #1 by revenue in China's healthcare intelligence market (~2.3% share of a highly fragmented market) and #1 in the 'emerging healthcare intelligence companies' sub-segment (~25.6% share); more recent (FY2025/26) market-share figures were not disclosed in the filings reviewed, but management continues to describe the company as a leading/pioneering player serving top-tier hospitals and regulators

moat_factors.description: Nearly 9 billion authorized medical records from 1.32 billion patient visits across 12,000+ hospitals, built over a decade; very difficult for a new entrant to replicate given data-access, privacy and hospital-relationship barriers

Clinical Assistant Copilot and AI Middle Platform are embedded directly in physician workstations at top hospitals; management explicitly argues this creates switching costs once tied to clinical pathways and administrative workflows

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory/relationship barriers with hospitals and regulators
moat_factors.description: Long-standing relationships with 133 top hospitals and 54 regulators/policymakers, and status as a founding partner of national AI pilot bases (Beijing, Henan), create incumbency advantages in a politically sensitive data domain

moat_factors.factor: Operating incumbency in city Hui Min Bao insurance programs
moat_factors.description: Sole/main operating platform for Beijing (5 years, 19m+ insured) and Shenzhen (4 years, 6m+ insured) inclusive insurance programs; renewal-based incumbency with high switching friction for city governments
17 of the top 20 multinational pharma companies are clients and 516+ clinical research projects completed, but this segment competes with well-capitalized global CROs and data companies

weaknesses: Still relatively small absolute scale (~RMB819m FY2026 revenue) versus global health-data/AI peers and against China's enormous but fragmented hospital market
History of heavy losses and cash burn (FY2022-FY2025 cumulative net losses exceeding RMB1.7bn) raises questions about the durability of newly achieved profitability
Revenue still substantially project/tender-based (especially AI for Medical regional government platforms), which is lumpy and dependent on public-sector budgets and tender timing
Life Sciences segment revenue declined year-on-year in H1 FY2026, showing exposure to pharma R&D spending cycles
Reliance on sensitive patient health data creates concentrated regulatory and reputational risk relative to less data-sensitive software peers

growth_drivers: Secular tailwind from Chinese government AI-in-healthcare policy push (national AI pilot bases, data-element monetization initiatives) driving hospital/regulator tender demand

Shift from project-based to reusable, disease-based platform/subscription revenue via scalable disease modules (oncology, diabetes, hematology, cardio/cerebrovascular) intended to improve revenue quality and margins

Large-scale rollout of intelligent agent ecosystem (Clinical Assistant Copilot 2.0, Yidu Smart Evidence) embedding AI more deeply into physician and hospital-admin workflows, which management expects to raise switching costs and average revenue per client

Expansion of Hui Min Bao inclusive-insurance and digital-therapeutics model (diabetes/chronic disease) into new provinces beyond Beijing/Shenzhen (e.g., Hainan, Shanxi, Tianjin), monetizing the existing 22m+ active user base
International/overseas expansion ('second growth curve') replicating national/regional platform delivery and disease-based/outcome-based payment models in new markets

Operating leverage: opex ratio (sales, admin, R&D as % of revenue) has fallen sharply (from 76% to 44.3% of revenue FY24-FY26), suggesting further margin expansion as revenue scales without proportional cost growth
Large net cash position (RMB2.08bn as of 31 March 2026) available to fund continued R&D investment, selective M&A, and the inaugural dividend signaling capital-return optionality

business.risk: Customer/tender concentration in government and top-tier hospital contracts
business.description: AI for Medical revenue depends on winning public-sector tenders (e.g., Hainan provincial platform, Henan AI pilot base) that are lumpy, competitively bid and subject to budget cycles
FY2026 was the company's first full-year profit after years of large losses (-RMB766m FY2022 to -RMB135m FY2025); sustainability of the turnaround through further quarters is unproven
Segment revenue fell 4.4% YoY in H1 FY2026, reflecting exposure to pharma/biotech R&D budget cycles and clinical-trial volumes

business.risk: Intensifying competition from both specialized rivals and large tech/software platforms entering medical AI
business.description: LinkDoc, Winning Health, Taimei and other domestic players, plus potential entry by larger Chinese tech/cloud firms with AI capabilities, could compress pricing and market share

financial.risk: History of negative operating cash flow
financial.description: Operating cash outflow only turned positive in H2 FY2026 (RMB29.3m); full-year operating cash flow was still negative (-RMB22.0m), and the long loss history consumed substantial cash before the recent narrowing

financial.risk: RMB currency exposure for HKD-denominated equity/dividend
financial.description: Reports in RMB but listed/traded in HKD; dividends (HK$0.04/share proposed FY2026) and equity value are subject to RMB/HKD translation

financial.risk: Receivables/working-capital risk from government and hospital clients
financial.description: Public-sector and hospital clients can have long payment cycles, affecting cash conversion despite revenue recognition

regulatory.description: Core business model depends on authorized access to patient-level medical records; tightening PRC data security, personal information protection (PIPL) or cross-border data rules could constrain data acquisition, usage rights or overseas expansion
Chinese hospital and pharma sector compliance crackdowns in recent years have periodically slowed tender activity and lengthened sales cycles industry-wide

regulatory.risk: Government healthcare-spending and insurance-fund policy shifts
regulatory.description: AI for Care segment depends on continuation and expansion of municipal Hui Min Bao programs and medical insurance fund settlement mechanisms set by local governments

regulatory.risk: US/HK listing and geopolitical scrutiny of Chinese data companies
regulatory.description: As a China-based health-data company, potential exposure to foreign investment, export-control, or delisting-related scrutiny applicable to sensitive-data Chinese issuers, though Yidu is HK-listed rather than US-listed

macro.description: Local government fiscal constraints could slow public hospital and regional platform tender spending, a key revenue driver for AI for Medical
AI for Life Sciences revenue is tied to multinational and domestic pharma clinical development budgets, which are sensitive to broader biotech funding cycles
Indirect effect on HKD-denominated share price and dividend from RMB-denominated earnings

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management and third-party commentary (Frost & Sullivan-style market framing in filings) describe China's medical AI/healthcare intelligence industry as moving from technology validation to large-scale deployment, with strong policy tailwinds (national AI pilot bases, 'data element' monetization initiatives) but a highly fragmented competitive landscape (Yidu's historical leading share was only low single digits of the overall market)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- AI for Medical tied to government/hospital capital and tender budgets (somewhat counter-cyclical/policy-driven); AI for Life Sciences tied to pharma R&D cycles (more cyclical); AI for Care tied to municipal insurance program renewals (relatively stable, multi-year contracts)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity; indirect effect through valuation of a growth/AI-thematic stock and through the yield on its large RMB2.08bn cash/deposit balance
key_input_costs: Compute/GPU and cloud infrastructure costs (including domestic Huawei GPUs and NVIDIA platforms)
Skilled AI/data-science and clinical-informatics talent (R&D headcount costs)
Data licensing/acquisition and hospital data-governance partnership costs

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual results announced (year ended 31 March 2026): first full-year net profit of RMB78.8 million, above prior guidance of RMB55-70 million; revenue up 14.6% to RMB819.3 million; gross margin improved to 36.4%; adjusted EBITDA grew roughly 4.6x to ~RMB220 million; stock surged over 15-17% on the news
Board proposed inaugural final dividend of HK$0.04 per share for FY2026, the company's first-ever dividend, alongside the turnaround to profitability
Full-year operating cash outflow narrowed 91.2% year-on-year; H2 FY2026 operating cash flow turned positive at RMB29.3 million for the first time

Interim results: revenue up 8.7% YoY to RMB358.1 million; net loss narrowed 72.0% YoY to RMB15.8 million; AI for Medical segment revenue up 14.6% and AI for Care up 30.3%, while AI for Life Sciences revenue declined 4.4% YoY; cash and deposits of RMB2,099.3 million maintained; no interim dividend declared
Company conducted 11 separate share buybacks during December 2025, totaling over HK$17.4 million
Founder/Chairlady Gong Yingying spoke at the World Economic Forum's 'Summer Davos' (Annual Meeting of the New Champions) in Dalian on a panel about access to innovative medicines
AGM scheduled to approve the FY2026 final dividend, director re-elections, auditor reappointment and share issuance mandates
Citi reiterated a Buy rating with an HK$11.00 price target (one of the few actively covering analysts)

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results (announced 2026-07-24) and H1 FY2026 Interim Report

items.metric: Net profit (prior-period guidance that was exceeded)
items.notes: Company had previously guided FY2026 net profit of RMB55-70 million; actual result of RMB78.8 million beat the upper end of that range

items.target: No explicit numerical FY2027 guidance disclosed in filings reviewed
items.notes: Management's qualitative outlook emphasizes continued order-volume growth, disease-based platform monetization and international expansion, but the FY2026 annual report and H1 FY2026 interim report reviewed did not contain specific quantitative FY2027 revenue, margin or profit targets

items.target: Continue shift toward disease-based, reusable platform revenue; expand intelligent-agent deployment; pursue international replication of platform model as a 'second growth curve'; maintain prudent capital allocation across R&D, M&A and shareholder returns
items.notes: These are directional/strategic priorities reiterated in both the FY2026 annual report Business Outlook section and prior filings, not quantified targets

guidance.management_commentary: Chairlady Gong Yingying characterized FY2026 as a 'historic turnaround from losses to profitability,' framing it as validation of the business model rather than short-term cost-cutting, and said the Board's dividend recommendation reflects confidence in cash generation while reaffirming continued R&D investment. Management's Business Outlook stresses continued focus on 'core clients, core diseases and core scenarios,' deeper embedding of AI into clinical/hospital-admin workflows to raise switching costs, and exploration of overseas markets as a second growth curve, while maintaining 'prudent capital allocation' across R&D, international expansion, M&A and shareholder returns.

bull_case: FY2026 marked an inflection to full-year GAAP profitability and improving operating cash flow (H2 turned positive), suggesting the long-loss-making growth phase may be ending and operating leverage is starting to show through as opex ratios fall sharply

Large, hard-to-replicate proprietary real-world medical data asset (9bn records, 1.32bn patient visits, 12,000+ hospitals) and growing embedding of AI tools directly into physician workflows (Clinical Assistant Copilot, Yidu Smart Evidence) could create durable switching costs and a widening moat as AI adoption in Chinese healthcare accelerates

Strong policy tailwinds from China's national AI-in-healthcare push (national AI pilot bases, data-element monetization initiatives) provide a structural multi-year demand driver for the AI for Medical segment

Balance sheet strength (RMB2.08bn cash/deposits versus modest debt) funds continued R&D, selective M&A and the newly initiated capital-return program (first-ever dividend plus share buybacks), reducing financing risk and signaling management confidence

Diversified three-segment model (hospitals/regulators, pharma, insurers/patients) with AI for Care growing fastest (+37.6% in FY2026) provides multiple avenues for growth beyond the historically volatile project-based hospital/government tender business
bear_case: Only one year of full-year profitability after six years of substantial losses (cumulative losses exceeding RMB1.7bn from FY2022-FY2025) makes it hard to confirm the turnaround is structural rather than a temporary cost-cutting-driven result

Revenue remains significantly tender/project-based (especially AI for Medical regional government platforms), exposing the company to lumpy order timing and Chinese local-government budget constraints

AI for Life Sciences, roughly a third of revenue, already showed a year-on-year revenue decline in H1 FY2026, indicating sensitivity to pharma R&D spending cycles and competitive pressure from global CRO/data players

Business model's dependence on sensitive patient health data creates concentrated and potentially intensifying PRC data-privacy/data-security regulatory risk that could constrain data access or increase compliance costs

Thin and recent analyst coverage (effectively one to two actively covering firms) combined with intensifying competition from both specialized Chinese rivals (LinkDoc, Winning Health, Taimei) and potential entrants (larger Chinese cloud/AI platforms) creates uncertainty about long-term market share and pricing power in a market where Yidu's own disclosed historical share was only low single digits
